clue.text: Small volume about one pursuing girl is a masterpiece

indicators.note: about means going round, so the small volume's letters wrap the rest

parts.note: CC, cubic centimetres, is a small measure of volume

indicators.note: pursuing means coming after, so the numeral follows the girl

parts.note: a lass is a girl
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A slim book about a man chasing a girl turns out to be a great work.
explanation.definitionFit: A classic is a work of lasting excellence, an acknowledged masterpiece.

clue.text: Roughly demonstrate housing co-operative's beginning to provide good source of income

parts.note: CA, circa, means roughly or approximately

indicators.note: housing means holding inside, so the word for demonstrate contains the letter

parts.note: to show is to demonstrate

indicators.note: beginning picks the first letter of co-operative's

explanation.surface: A rough demonstration about a co-op starting to bring in money.
explanation.definitionFit: A cash cow is a business or product that reliably yields profit, an idiom for a steady earner.

clue.text: Conscious of key deficiency in American state

indicators.note: a deficiency in something means it lacks a part, so the key's letters are missing from the state

parts.note: Delaware is a state of the USA
DEL is the delete key on a computer keyboard

explanation.surface: Someone aware that a key resource is lacking in a US state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key' looks like a musical key or A, but it is the DEL key on a keyboard.
explanation.definitionFit: To be conscious of something is to know of it; the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Replace great player expected to do well on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio means heard rather than read, so the words sound like the entry

parts.words: great player expected to do well
parts.note: super means great; a seed is a player ranked to go far in a tournament

explanation.surface: A star player tipped to win is replaced, and it is reported on air.
explanation.walkthrough: SUPER SEED, said aloud, sounds like the entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To supersede is to take the place of, a synonym of replace.

clue.text: Twist around, beginning to dance, twist around as part of health regimen?

indicators.note: around means the twist word wraps everything that follows

parts.note: to coil is to twist

indicators.note: around#2 means the Dickens character's name goes round the dance letter

parts.note: Oliver Twist is the Dickens orphan, so twist stands for his first name

indicators.note: beginning to picks the first letter of dance

explanation.surface: Instructions for a dance routine, twisting about, as part of a fitness plan.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated 'twist around' looks like one instruction twice, but the first 'Twist' is a verb and the second names the Dickens orphan.
explanation.definitionFit: Cod-liver oil is a traditional dietary supplement taken for health, so it is one example of a regimen element.

clue.text: Fantastic beast improvising back to front

indicators.note: back to front means the final letter is shifted to the start

parts.note: riffing is improvising, as a musician does

explanation.surface: A musician jamming a tune backwards produces a monster.
explanation.definitionFit: The griffin is a mythical creature with an eagle's head and a lion's body.

clue.text: See 14
Stop working to support trendy record company

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits below the other

parts.note: in means fashionable or trendy
a machine that dies stops working

explanation.surface: Someone stops work to back a fashionable label.
explanation.definitionFit: An indie is an independent record label, one not owned by a major company.

clue.text: Old Labour leader's image making an impression on the ground

parts.note: Michael Foot led the British Labour Party from 1980 to 1983
a print is a picture or image

explanation.surface: A former Labour leader's picture leaves a mark on the public.
explanation.definitionFit: A footprint is the mark a foot leaves pressed into the ground.

clue.text: Is aware of vocal newspaper's material assistance for those stricken by cold

definitions.text: material assistance for those stricken by cold

indicators.note: vocal means spoken, so the word for being aware is heard, not spelt

parts.note: knows means is aware of
a rag is a disparaging word for a newspaper

explanation.surface: A newspaper speaks up about giving material help to people hit by cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'material assistance' reads as financial aid but is literally a piece of cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A nose-rag is slang for a handkerchief, cloth that helps anyone with a head cold.

clue.text: Steps made in a chaotic way

definitions.text: Steps made in a chaotic way

indicators.note: in a chaotic way says the letters of the two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Footsteps taken in disorder describe a panicked rush.
explanation.definitionFit: Stampedes are panicked mass rushes, chaotic steps taken by a herd or crowd.

clue.text: Refuse right to sleep rough outside

indicators.note: outside means the sleeping word goes round the abbreviation

parts.note: to doss is British slang for sleeping rough or in makeshift quarters

explanation.surface: A homeless person declines the right to sleep on the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' reads as a verb but is the noun, rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Dross is worthless matter or rubbish, a synonym of the noun refuse.

clue.text: Raise your glass, knocking back Southern Comfort

indicators.note: knocking back means knocking off the back, so the last letter goes

parts.note: cheers is the toast said when raising a glass

explanation.surface: A toast to a drinker downing a Southern Comfort, the American whiskey liqueur.
explanation.walkthrough: Southern Comfort is a liqueur, but the words split: one gives S, the other is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To cheer someone is to comfort or hearten them; both are verbs of consolation.

clue.text: Host target area surrounds board

indicators.note: surrounds means the target word goes round the board word

parts.note: the inner is the ring just outside the bull on an archery or darts target
keep means board, food and lodging, as in earning one's keep

explanation.surface: A host aiming at a target with a board in the way.
explanation.definitionFit: An innkeeper is the landlord of an inn, who acts as host to guests.

clue.text: Dull, vain don abused invalid

indicators.note: abused means misused or knocked about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A boring, conceited academic mistreats a sick person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invalid' reads as a sick person but is the adjective, not valid.
explanation.definitionFit: Null and void is a legal phrase for having no force, the same as invalid.

clue.text: One couldn't appreciate wife when time at home got hard following gossip

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the hardening word comes after the gossip word

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
in means at home
gas is idle chatter or gossip
to set is to harden, as concrete or jelly does

explanation.surface: A man fails to value his wife when, back home, she hardens after gossip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appreciate' reads as value emotionally but means rise in value.
explanation.definitionFit: A wasting asset, such as a lease, loses value over time and so cannot grow in worth.

clue.text: Carrot cake may use this instead of sugar

definitions.text: Carrot cake may use this instead of sugar

parts.words: Carrot cake may use this instead of sugar
parts.note: read as baking it is a sugar substitute; carrot also suggests an inducement, so a bribe is hinted

explanation.surface: A baking tip about sugar substitutes in carrot cake.
explanation.definitionFit: A sugar substitute used in baking, and also, figuratively, an inducement or bribe.

clue.text: Enduring riddle of silent grave

indicators.note: to riddle is to pierce with holes or sift, so the words are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: The mystery of a quiet tomb lasts forever.
explanation.definitionFit: Everlasting means lasting forever, a synonym of enduring.

clue.text: Move desk to turn bolt

indicators.note: move means shift the letters of desk around

parts.note: milk that turns goes off; addle similarly means go rotten

explanation.surface: Instructions to shift a desk so the bolt can be turned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bolt' looks like a fastening but is the verb, flee.
explanation.definitionFit: To skedaddle is to run away hastily, a colloquial synonym of bolt.

clue.text: Year the euro collapsed, just as I predicted

indicators.note: collapsed means fallen apart, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An economist gloating about the year the single currency fell apart.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'there you are' is said when something turns out as foretold, like 'I told you so'.

clue.text: Redevelopment of top site makes little impression on the ground

definitions.text: makes little impression on the ground

indicators.note: redevelopment means rebuilding, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Redeveloping a prime site barely changes the land.
explanation.definitionFit: To tiptoe is to walk on the toes, quietly, leaving hardly any mark underfoot.

clue.text: See 14
Incubator's going to replace energy source and work without interruption

indicators.note: to replace means the going word takes the place of the energy letter

parts.note: a nest is where eggs are incubated

indicators.note: source means where the word starts, so the first letter of energy is taken

parts.note: on means going, as in 'the show is on'
op, short for opus, is a musical work

explanation.surface: A hen goes on laying, replacing her energy and working all day.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonstop means continuing with no break or pause.

clue.text: Was on the beat as tap dancing got under way

indicators.note: dancing means moving about, so the letters of tap shift

parts.note: rolled means started moving, as cameras or a convoy roll

explanation.surface: A tap dancer keeps time as the show begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the beat' suggests music but means a police officer's round.
explanation.definitionFit: A police officer on the beat walks a set route; patrolled is that action in the past tense.

clue.text: Love meat mostly containing a bit of saturated fat

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O

indicators.note: containing means the shortened meat holds the letter inside
mostly means not quite all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: beef is a meat

indicators.note: a bit of picks the first letter of saturated

explanation.surface: Loving meat with saturated fat in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Obese means very overweight; fat is a plain synonym.

clue.text: Plug in contact with outside of lead for record deck

parts.note: an ad, advert, is a plug for a product

indicators.note: outside of means the contact word goes round the letter

parts.note: on means touching or in contact with

indicators.note: lead for picks the first letter of record

explanation.surface: Wiring a plug to the lead of a turntable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'record deck' looks like one item; 'deck' alone is the verb, decorate.
explanation.definitionFit: To adorn is to decorate, as halls are decked with holly.

clue.text: Ignominy of political leader being removed from platform

indicators.note: being removed from means the letter is taken out of the platform word

parts.note: a podium is a raised platform for a speaker

indicators.note: leader picks the first letter of political

explanation.surface: The disgrace of a party leader pushed off the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Odium is general hatred or disgrace attached to someone, close to ignominy.

clue.text: Cat jumps out of its skin

indicators.note: out of its skin means stripped of its outer letters

parts.note: bounces means jumps

explanation.surface: A cat jumping out of its skin in fright.
explanation.definitionFit: The ounce is another name for the snow leopard, a big cat.

clue.text: Extravagant words in newspaper's really cool blanket coverage

indicators.note: extravagant means wildly over the top, so the letters run wild

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times, a British newspaper

explanation.surface: Effusive praise in the paper for some very trendy blanket reporting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blanket coverage' suggests media saturation; here it is a literal cold covering.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep bank of snow blankets the ground and is very cold, a playful description.

clue.text: See 14
Auntie frustrated about covering too much stuff

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the concealed letters are read right to left
covering means the words hold the letters within them

explanation.surface: An aunt annoyed at having to look after far too many things.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters TIEFRUS sit inside 'Auntie frustrated'; 'about' turns them round.
explanation.definitionFit: A surfeit is an excess, an overabundance of something.

clue.text: Imagine 'cougar' meeting resistance in boy on the rebound!

indicators.note: on the rebound means bouncing back, so the whole is read backwards

parts.note: the cougar is also called the puma

indicators.note: in means the resistance letter goes inside the boy's name

parts.note: Ed is a boy's name
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Picture an older woman taking up with a young man after a breakup.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'cougar' is slang for an older woman dating younger men, hence the quotes; here it is just the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: To dream up is to invent or imagine something.
